dedupe_keys.name: wrap wildfire risk aware operation planning with a surrogate model of ignition risk from power lines under extreme weather

description: WRAP, the Wildfire Risk Aware operation planning Problem, is a method proposed in a 2021 arXiv paper (revised July 2022) to help utilities decide which segments of a power network to de-energise in California-style Public Safety Power Shut-offs, which are used to cut the chance of wildfire ignition by power lines during extreme weather. Sustained wind and wind gust can cause conductor clashing that could ignite surrounding vegetation. The authors use 3D non-linear vibration equations of power lines to generate a dataset covering physical, structural and meteorological parameters, then use machine learning to obtain a surrogate model that quantifies the ignition risk of individual lines, and embed it in an operation planning problem for system operators. The abstract reports that the cases show superior performance of WRAP under extreme weather. Access: the arXiv page; no code repository is stated on the abstract page; the paper is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Caveats: a research method, with outputs depending on the simulated conductor data and case systems. It suits wildfire risk and shut-off planning, and relates to the CPUC fire-threat map catalogued here.
